normative_action: The code-reviewer subagent performs an independent read-only review and never edits files; Write, Edit, MultiEdit and NotebookEdit are disallowed tools.
trigger_scope: code-reviewer subagent (PR review, diff review, pre-merge review, second-pass review of completed work)
exceptions: Bash is not tool-disallowed; the no-edit duty for shell use rests on the instruction text.

normative_action: The code-reviewer uses the code-review skill as the canonical procedure (preloaded; load it first if not loaded) and follows its scope, priorities and output format instead of redefining review criteria.
The code-reviewer reads the rule files that govern the changed paths before judging them, because the delegated context does not inherit the main session's loaded rules.
The code-reviewer runs the full security-scan only when the user asked for a security audit, the change is materially security-sensitive, or a concrete finding justifies broader investigation.
The reviewer returns the code-review output: findings ordered by severity, or an explicit statement that no meaningful findings exist plus the areas that could not be verified.

Project references point inward: domain model references no application project; use-case layer references only the domain model; implementation layer references the use-case layer and domain model; the entry point references the use-case layer and the implementation layer (the latter only for composition); never Domain -> Application, Domain -> Infrastructure or Application -> Infrastructure; a production project never references a test project. If a feature seems to need an outward reference, reconsider the abstraction boundary.
modality: MUST (architecture check: check-architecture.mjs exit 1; manifest hook reports architecture findings after .csproj changes)
trigger_scope: backend .csproj projects matched to roles by name pattern
exceptions: The check spec also allows entry point -> domain model; projects matching no role and unresolved references only produce warnings.

normative_action: Inner roles (domain model, use-case layer) must not reference the web-framework shared framework Microsoft.AspNetCore.App, whether through FrameworkReference, the Web SDK (implicit reference) or Microsoft.AspNetCore.* packages.

Do not give a backend test project broader production references than its test scope needs; keep the inward discipline (typical: Application.Tests -> Application and Domain as needed; IntegrationTests -> Api; optional Domain.Tests -> Domain; optional Infrastructure.Tests -> Infrastructure); the architecture check warns about references beyond the typical set of the test role.
exceptions: The mechanical check reports warnings only, not violations.

normative_action: A separate top-level tests/ directory is not created; backend tests live under backend/.
MediatR and Kommand packages require approval because mediator-based organization is not adopted; the manifest hook reports them and asks to remove them unless the user approved them.

Physical structure follows actual responsibilities: create only directories and projects that contain real code (layout trees are targets, not checklists); no speculative projects, infrastructure, empty directory trees, or generic Common/Helpers/Utils/Models buckets; optional folders (external-service abstractions, Middleware, Extensions, test projects) appear only once real need exists.

Keep backend production and test projects (backend/<Name>.<Layer>/), the frontend workspace (frontend/<Name>.Web/) and documentation (docs/) clearly separated in the approved layout; frontend tests stay inside the frontend workspace.
DDD-oriented directories (ValueObjects, DomainServices, Events, Exceptions) appear only when an approved design needs them; business rules or workflow behavior alone do not justify them.

Persistence and external-service abstractions (repository interfaces, IUnitOfWork, IEmailSender etc.) are defined in the use-case layer (Application) when use cases need them; implementation details stay out of Application.
Application must not use persistence-implementation types or APIs (persistence context and entity-set types, ORM APIs, database-provider types) or web-framework/transport implementation types.

Keep registration near the owning layer: AddApplication() registers Application services and validation only; AddInfrastructure(configuration) registers persistence (incl. the persistence context), repositories, the commit boundary, adapters, outbound HTTP integrations and resilience handlers; Api composes them.
Program.cs in the entry-point project is the composition root; it calls the layer registration methods and may register implementation-layer implementations.

NuGet Central Package Management: versions live only in Directory.Packages.props; project PackageReference entries are versionless (never duplicate a central version; generated versions are moved), VersionOverride only for a concrete reported reason; packages sit in the narrowest project that needs them; ManagePackageVersionsCentrally stays true.
exceptions: VersionOverride with a concrete reported reason.

normative_action: Changing a capability selection (changing the architecture frame, replacing a leaf implementation, changing the database provider inside persistence, clearing the optional frontend) or replacing approved baseline technology is Reserved and needs explicit approval through a Decision Request.

String semantics are product behavior when observable (case sensitivity, collation, culture vs ordinal comparison, normalization, trimming, uniqueness, lookup); when approved sources do not define them, ask for approval before choosing, including choices made implicitly through database or framework defaults; relying on the provider's default collation for observable behavior and changing observable string comparison (e.g. through a provider change) need approval.

Package additions and updates go only through the add-dependency workflow (concrete need, approved technology, latest stable compatible version, deprecation, vulnerability and license checks, approval for commercial or unclear licenses); the PreToolUse hook denies dependency-changing shell commands (dotnet add/remove package, dotnet package add/remove/update, dotnet tool install/update/uninstall, npm/pnpm/yarn mutations, the frontend CLI's ng add/update, PowerShell *-Package cmdlets) once with a pointer to the workflow.
modality: MUST (PreToolUse hook: first attempt denied, fails closed)
trigger_scope: Bash and PowerShell commands; package installation in backend and frontend
exceptions: The identical command is allowed when retried within 30 minutes (the hook cannot verify that the workflow ran); file edits of manifests are not gated before execution.

normative_action: NUnit is the default .NET test framework; in an established project that deliberately uses another framework follow that convention; do not introduce a second test framework without a concrete reason; xunit, MSTest and TUnit packages are reported as requiring approval and to be removed unless approved.
trigger_scope: backend test projects and NuGet manifests
exceptions: The hook escalates 'concrete reason' to user approval.

normative_action: Frontend baseline: current stable Angular created with the current Angular CLI, which selects compatible TypeScript and RxJS versions (TypeScript is not upgraded beyond Angular's supported range independently); standalone APIs, strict mode, routing, zoneless when supported, SCSS, Angular Material and CDK, Vitest.
Use npm ci for clean installs from the maintained lockfile (CI, fresh clone).
trigger_scope: frontend installs in CI and fresh clones

normative_action: Inspect package.json before running frontend commands; use scripts that exist (lint only when configured) and never invent script names.
Playwright is the approved E2E tool when frontend E2E coverage is required; it is not part of the minimal baseline scaffold.

Repairs must not weaken verification or bypass the root cause: no converting code to any to silence the compiler, disabling strict mode, suppressing diagnostics or tests without understanding them, or speculative framework workarounds.

Do not add NgRx, Axios, Lodash, Bootstrap, Tailwind or additional form, component or state-management libraries by default (or to bypass a local issue); use built-in Angular capabilities first and add an overlapping library only for a concrete need; the manifest hook reports listed packages (@ngrx/, @ngxs/, axios, lodash, bootstrap, @ng-bootstrap/, ngx-bootstrap, primeng, tailwindcss) as requiring a concrete need and approval.
modality: MUST NOT (manifest hook finding: concrete need and approval)

normative_action: Use the actual database provider when relational or provider behavior matters; real-provider test containers (Testcontainers.MsSql) are optional and added only when isolated real-provider tests justify them; never claim provider fidelity from a different provider (EF Core InMemory, SQLite).

When an approved CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md change affects schema constraints, indexes, column lengths or other persistence metadata: update the mapping, create a new migration when the schema changes (regenerate or edit only an unapplied, uncommitted migration per the normal workflow; do not casually alter existing migrations), verify Development seeding remains valid, and add or update persistence/integration tests when provider-specific behavior matters.
Production schema changes are an explicit deployment step; local database update/drop commands are for Development only and never point at Production.

When representative Development data already exists it is left unchanged: migrating an existing Development database does not require the seeder to patch rows, and developers recreate the local database explicitly when they need a fresh dataset.
Inner roles (domain model, use-case layer) must not reference persistence-implementation packages (Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore*).
Before non-trivial changes inspect the relevant code and apply the governing rules; workflow facets direct reading the applicable rule files first when they have not loaded with the touched paths.

Whenever a domain-model or persistence change affects seeded entities (new required or removed/renamed properties, relationships, enum/status values, states, invariants), update the maintained DbSeeder in the same change and review it together with migrations touching seeded entities; the Stop hook reminds when model files changed without a seeder change.
modality: MUST (Stop hook reminder: blocks stopping once per change state)
exceptions: Reminder is Git-only and shown once per material state.

normative_action: Treat migrations as source code: review every generated migration before committing it, especially destructive schema changes, unexpected column recreation, data migrations, indexes, foreign keys and delete behavior.

Seed data must stay valid for the migrated schema and current domain model: seed entities preserve current domain invariants and valid relationships; prefer readable deterministic examples over exhaustive or random combinations.

Build the affected projects and run relevant tests (for persistence changes list or script pending migrations to confirm the expected schema change); a build failure means the implementation is not complete.

For persistence/startup changes verify Development composition at runtime: apply migrations to a local Development database explicitly, start the API in Development and confirm the seeder populates an empty database or leaves an existing one unchanged.

When resilience is required use Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience for HttpClient or Microsoft.Extensions.Resilience for other pipelines; direct Polly usage is an explicit, documented exception and the Polly package is reported as requiring approval.
modality: DEFAULT (manifest hook finding: approval required for Polly)

normative_action: Manual mapping for simple cases; Mapster (+ Mapster.DependencyInjection) is the approved mapping library when mapping volume warrants it; another mapping framework (AutoMapper) is a Reserved library addition reported as requiring approval.
modality: DEFAULT (manifest hook finding: approval required for AutoMapper)

normative_action: Select the latest stable compatible version verified from the registry; never floating versions (*, latest, x, empty) and no prerelease versions unless explicitly requested; the manifest hook reports floating and prerelease versions in Directory.Packages.props and package.json.
trigger_scope: NuGet and npm additions and updates
exceptions: Prerelease explicitly requested; MSBuild-property versions are only flagged for manual confirmation.

normative_action: Slot contract completeness: a slot implementation supplies every required facet of its slot contract with the stated form, level, loading and content (architecture: style, boundaries, layout, check; backend-testing: framework rule, commands, enforcement adapter, knowledge skill; frontend when selected: framework, stack, commands, enforcement, knowledge; persistence: access, seeding, dev-config, workflow, commands, enforcement, knowledge) and the frame expresses every role of roles.md without contradicting a role-level rule; a missing required facet is a conformance failure raised as a Decision Request instead of shipping the module.
trigger_scope: creating or replacing a slot implementation (template maintenance, architecture-decision)
why_extra_or_uncertain: Template capability-contract structure; no oracle policy requires an implementation to ship enforcement data, command facets or knowledge skills, or defines conformance of instruction modules.

normative_action: Leak rule: outside an implementation module (its manifest-listed facet files and module directory), instruction artifacts refer to slot concerns only by slot name, facet role (<slot>.<facet>) and the stable role vocabulary; implementation names appear only in the selection record and the instruction map; workflows reach implementation-specific steps through facet roles and must not hardcode selected implementations; leaf slots depend on roles, not frame terms.
exceptions: Module-owned facets; the selection record (decisions.md capability selection) and INSTRUCTION_MAP.md.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Instruction-authoring vocabulary rule of the L1 capability design; no oracle policy restricts which technology names may appear in which instruction files.

normative_action: Content ownership in the capability model: placement belongs to the architecture frame and technique to leaf modules; implementation-independent policy (test policy, frontend structure, browser security, package-manager conventions) stays outside modules in neutral rules; frame facets keep leaf technology out; leaf bindings that cannot be expressed through roles are declared as binds: in the leaf manifest (persistence requires a binds: declaration to the selected frame).
trigger_scope: template content placement during maintenance or capability replacement
why_extra_or_uncertain: Template-structure ownership rule; the oracle prescribes no ownership location for instruction content.

normative_action: A capability-selection change (changing the frame, replacing a leaf implementation or provider, clearing or adding the optional frontend) requires an ADR recorded with architecture-decision in addition to Reserved approval.
why_extra_or_uncertain: ARC-020/DEP-002/GOV-017 require explicit approval for replacing approved technology but no oracle policy requires an ADR artifact for the change.

normative_action: Replacement and removal procedure: replacing a slot implementation replaces all of its facets together (rule facet, commands, enforcement data, knowledge content, selection row; for the frame also the CLAUDE.md style import) and keeps neutral rules such as roles.md unchanged unless the role vocabulary itself changes (Reserved); workflows refer only to facets and need no edits; removing the optional frontend sets its selection row to none, deletes every manifest-listed file and the module directory, removes the frontend-stack import from CLAUDE.md and the module rows from the instruction map; every replacement or removal ends with a passing check-instructions run.
trigger_scope: template maintenance: capability replacement and removal
why_extra_or_uncertain: Template maintenance procedure of the capability model; no oracle policy governs how instruction files change when a technology is replaced or removed.

normative_action: Persistence semantics on change: the persistence selection records declared properties (provider variant, default string-comparison/case-sensitivity semantics, migration mechanism, seeding mechanism); replacing the implementation (e.g. an ORM by a micro-ORM) must not silently lose migration or seeding semantics and the new module states its mechanisms explicitly; a database-provider change is a variation inside the persistence slot that updates the declared properties, persistence.dev-config, the relational-fidelity binding and commands.
why_extra_or_uncertain: ARC-020 requires approval for new persistence technology and GOV-006 for observable string semantics, but no oracle policy requires preserving migration/seeding mechanisms or maintaining a declared-property record when persistence changes.

normative_action: When the schema changes, add a migration from the implementation-layer project with the entry-point project as startup project; the Stop hook reminds when domain-model or persistence-configuration files changed without a migration change and asks to confirm that no schema change is needed.
modality: MUST (workflow step) / SHOULD (Stop hook reminder, blocks stopping once per change state)
exceptions: Git-only; once per material state; continuation caused by the hook is not re-blocked.
why_extra_or_uncertain: The oracle requires a migration only for schema-affecting CUSTOM_SETTINGS changes (PST-009) and review of generated migrations (PST-010); it has no general duty to pair every schema change with a migration or to confirm schema impact at stop time.

normative_action: The persistence change procedure reports model changes, migration names with review notes (destructive operations called out), whether DbSeeder was updated or unaffected, and the tests added or updated.
why_extra_or_uncertain: WF-009 requires reporting the actual verification state; it does not prescribe persistence-specific report contents.

normative_action: Packages Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Polly, Polly.Extensions.Http (deprecated resilience integrations), FluentValidation.AspNetCore (deprecated automatic-validation integration) and Serilog.Sinks.Elasticsearch (deprecated sink) must not be added; the manifest hook reports them as 'must not be added'.
modality: MUST NOT (manifest hook finding after the change; no approval path)
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-004 requires checking deprecation and DEP-020 treats direct Polly integration as an explicit exception, but no oracle policy forbids specific packages outright regardless of approval.

normative_action: Do not use npm --force or --legacy-peer-deps merely to bypass incompatible peer dependencies; resolve the actual compatibility problem. The PreToolUse hook detects --force, -f, --legacy-peer-deps (and npm config set force/legacy-peer-deps) on npm/pnpm/yarn install-like commands and asks the user to confirm.
modality: MUST NOT (PreToolUse hook: asks the user)
exceptions: Proceeds when the user explicitly confirms.

normative_action: When SPECIFICATION.md or CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md changes, keep the two consistent and run the custom-settings workflow to synchronize affected code, validation, configuration, tests, documentation and frontend.
modality: SHOULD (PostToolUse feedback after edits; Stop reminder once per change state)
exceptions: Stop reminder only in a Git working tree and once per material state.

normative_action: When backend production C# files changed without any backend test change, confirm existing coverage, regression tests for bug fixes and preservation of behavioral probes (verify) before finishing, or state briefly why it does not apply.
modality: SHOULD (Stop hook reminder: blocks stopping once per change state)
trigger_scope: Stop event in a Git working tree
exceptions: Once per material state; outside Git only an advisory system message; a continuation caused by the hook is not re-blocked.

normative_action: Dependency-removal commands (npm/pnpm uninstall, remove, rm, un, unlink; yarn remove; dotnet remove package; dotnet package remove; dotnet tool uninstall; Uninstall-Package) are treated as dependency changes: the hook denies them once and routes them to the add-dependency workflow.
exceptions: The identical command passes when retried within 30 minutes.
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-001..DEP-005 govern additions and updates; no oracle policy routes dependency removals through a workflow gate.

normative_action: Changing the project reference graph is Reserved unless it implements the approved layout: every dotnet add/remove reference and dotnet reference add/remove command requires user confirmation, and removing or moving a .csproj is reported as a Reserved change of the project set/reference graph.
modality: REQUIRES_APPROVAL (Reserved; PreToolUse hook asks on every reference command; manifest hook reports removed or moved project files)
exceptions: Changes implementing the approved layout (project-structure) are not Reserved, but the hook asks anyway because it cannot tell; direct .csproj edits are only checked afterwards by the architecture check.
why_extra_or_uncertain: ARC-020 requires approval for new layers/projects and ARC-001 constrains direction; no oracle policy makes individual reference edges between existing projects (including direction-legal edges outside the documented layout) Reserved, nor requires confirmation of each reference command.

normative_action: Write clear, correct code first; add specialized optimizations only for a concrete reason, preferring measurement or profiling evidence for non-trivial ones.

Introduce compiled queries, allocation-reducing return types (ValueTask), pooling, custom serialization, aggressive caching or raw SQL for performance only for a measured or clearly demonstrated need.
Keep database work efficient: filter and project in the database when practical, avoid unnecessary round trips, over-fetching and N+1 patterns, and paginate potentially large result sets.
Use async APIs for asynchronous I/O and never block them with synchronous waits (.Result, .Wait(), .GetAwaiter().GetResult()) or similar sync-over-async patterns.

Propagate cancellation tokens through asynchronous operations when cancellation is meaningful (at the entry point HttpContext.RequestAborted); do not add cancellation parameters to purely synchronous code without a use case.

Use an injectable time abstraction (TimeProvider; tests FakeTimeProvider) for logic that depends on the current clock and needs deterministic tests; do not mechanically replace stored or explicit timestamps.
Never create and dispose a new HTTP client instance per request; use a factory-managed client (IHttpClientFactory, typed or named clients) or another appropriate long-lived strategy.
External I/O calls have a bounded execution time appropriate to the operation; avoid overlapping timeout mechanisms whose combined behavior is unclear.
Retry only when repeating the operation is safe; never automatically retry state-changing operations without idempotency or another concrete duplicate-prevention mechanism.
Respect Retry-After or equivalent rate-limit guidance where appropriate; never retry indefinitely or aggressively.
Use fallback only when the fallback result is semantically acceptable; never hide correctness failures behind convenient default values.
Caller cancellation is not a transient dependency failure: never retry it or convert it into repeated outbound attempts.
Caching is not a default architectural requirement; introduce it only for a clear measured or reasoned need and choose the implementation by deployment, consistency and staleness requirements.
Cache keys uniquely represent the cached value and include the relevant user, tenant, locale and query dimensions; never use global keys for user- or tenant-specific data.
Every cache entry has a lifetime or another explicit invalidation strategy.
Invalidate or update cache entries only consistently with successful underlying mutations; the cache is never a second source of truth.

Use strongly typed options for structured service configuration (IOptions<T> bound with AddOptions<T>().Bind), validated at startup (ValidateOnStart) when missing or invalid values prevent correct or secure operation; avoid scattered string-based configuration lookups.
Use constructor injection for required dependencies; avoid service-locator and property-injection patterns.
Respect service lifetimes: never capture a shorter-lived dependency inside a longer-lived service.
Log through the injected logging abstraction (ILogger<T>) with structured message templates and stable property names; avoid string interpolation that turns structured values into opaque text.
Follow the repository's conventions and .editorconfig; use modern C# when it improves clarity, but do not mechanically modernize working code.

For new code prefer file-scoped namespaces when consistent with the project, keep one primary top-level type per matching file, and use the Async suffix for task-returning (awaitable) methods unless an existing or framework contract makes that inappropriate.
Do not perform style-only rewrites outside the requested change unless explicitly asked.
Add a dependency only for a concrete current requirement; never install packages for hypothetical future use.
Keep pages and components focused on presentation and UI orchestration; do not move trivial presentation logic into services merely to shrink components.

Keep backend communication in explicit feature data-access services; do not scatter HTTP client calls through presentation components and never import backend domain or persistence types into the frontend.
Frontend structure stays feature-oriented: avoid application-wide technical buckets and empty architecture folders, keep feature-specific code inside its feature, keep core/shared small.
Use route-level lazy loading for meaningful features; do not lazy-load every tiny component.
Prefer simple local, component or service state before introducing a state-management library.
Follow the documented API error contract: centralize reusable problem-details parsing when practical and never infer business behavior from human-readable exception messages.

Use reactive forms for non-trivial forms when explicit state, validation and testability help; frontend validation improves UX but never replaces backend validation or data-integrity and security enforcement.

Return problem-details responses (RFC 9457; ProblemDetails via AddProblemDetails) for non-validation HTTP failures and validation problem-details (ValidationProblemDetails, automatic [ApiController] response) for request validation; keep machine-readable error contracts stable and safe.
Choose 200/201/202/204 by actual HTTP semantics: never 200 for every outcome, 201 merely because a row was inserted internally, or 202 for work that already completed.
A successful collection query with zero matches returns 200 with an empty collection, not 404.
Use 401 when authentication is missing or failed and 403 when an authenticated principal is not permitted; returning 404 to hide protected resources requires a deliberate, consistent security policy.
Use 409 for a valid request that conflicts with current state and 412 when an explicit HTTP precondition such as If-Match fails.
Unexpected failures propagate to one centralized exception-handling boundary (IExceptionHandler with AddExceptionHandler/UseExceptionHandler); avoid repetitive catch/log/rethrow blocks.
Never expose stack traces, SQL, connection strings, internal paths, secret values or sensitive exception details in public API errors.
Do not establish business exceptions as the default architecture, and do not throw and catch exceptions to jump between normal expected branches.
Log an unexpected exception once, at the boundary that handles it, not again in repository, use-case, entry-point and global handler.
Normal client-request cancellation (OperationCanceledException with RequestAborted signaled) is not a server failure: never map it to a generic 500 or log it as an unhandled application error.
Do not introduce API versioning merely because an API exists; add it when published compatibility or coexisting client generations create a concrete need.
Once external clients rely on an API version, avoid silent breaking changes: a breaking contract change requires a new version or another explicitly approved compatibility strategy.
When explicit versioning is required, use one strategy consistently: URL-segment versioning unless project requirements justify another.
Health checks stay cheap and deterministic: never full business workflows, expensive queries or mutating database work.
Liveness avoids external dependencies whose outage could cause restart loops; readiness may depend on capabilities required to serve traffic and reflects startup and dependency availability.
Publicly reachable health responses must not expose secrets, credentials, connection details, stack traces or unnecessary internal diagnostics.
Never hardcode or commit real secrets, credentials, private keys, access/refresh tokens or production connection strings, including in example or Development configuration files.

Use a local secret mechanism in development (dotnet user-secrets) and environment-specific injection or a managed secret store in deployed environments; do not assume a cloud provider the project has not chosen.

Treat data crossing the trusted boundary (HTTP requests, uploads, external-service responses, message payloads, user-supplied identifiers and filters) as untrusted and validate it at the owning layer where assumptions matter.
Use parameterized database access; never build SQL by concatenating untrusted input.
Do not trust client-provided file metadata such as MIME type as authoritative when upload handling or security decisions depend on actual content.
Enforce authorization on the server; frontend route guards, hidden or disabled buttons and client checks are UX, not a security boundary.
Anonymous access is deliberate and visible; avoid redundant authorization attributes when a secure global or fallback policy already expresses the intent.

Do not implement custom token or password security, password hashing or reset-token cryptography when the platform's established authentication and identity facilities (ASP.NET Core authentication handlers, ASP.NET Core Identity) cover the requirement.
For Bearer/OIDC authentication validate what the actual issuer requires (issuer, audience where applicable, signature/signing authority, lifetime); never disable validation to make a token work.
Do not expose authentication-failure detail that unnecessarily reveals secrets or account state; login behavior avoids account-enumeration leaks where relevant.
When browser cookies carry authentication credentials automatically, include CSRF protection in the design; do not assume the frontend framework removes the risk.
Do not claim any browser token-storage mechanism is universally secure; choose storage by the application's threat model; tokens are never logged.

Production traffic carrying credentials or sensitive data uses TLS; respect the actual hosting topology (TLS may terminate at a proxy) and never disable certificate validation to make an integration work.
Configure CORS as the narrowest policy satisfying actual browser-client requirements; never combine credentialed cross-origin requests with unrestricted origins.

Do not implement custom cryptography when a well-reviewed platform mechanism fits; do not treat the platform's application payload-protection API (ASP.NET Core Data Protection, short-lived payloads) as universal database encryption.

Never log passwords, access/refresh tokens, private keys, authentication secrets or full payment credentials; avoid PII without a concrete permitted operational need; log level is not a privacy control.
Do not serialize arbitrary request bodies, domain objects or sensitive payloads into logs by default; log the minimum operationally useful non-sensitive context.
Security-sensitive authorization, permission and required-control checks fail safely; never silently convert a lookup or configuration failure into success.
When a required security control cannot be configured correctly, prefer a visible startup/configuration failure over an insecure fallback.

Choose the narrowest test level that meaningfully verifies the behavior (unit tests for isolated logic, integration tests when framework wiring, HTTP, persistence, serialization, authentication or component interaction is the subject); no fixed unit/integration ratio is required.

Test observable behavior, not implementation details: tests survive internal refactoring; do not assert private calls or incidental call sequences or reproduce the implementation's algorithm; interaction checks only when the interaction is the specified behavior.

Tests are deterministic, independent of execution order and isolated from Production and Development data, uncontrolled external systems, shared mutable state and (where an injectable time abstraction allows) wall-clock timing.

For small finite input/state spaces list explicit declarative cases (an NUnit [TestCase] row; TestCaseSource counts as generated case machinery) instead of loops, branching, LINQ or generated case machinery inside tests, and state expected results instead of computing them.

Use in-process host integration tests (WebApplicationFactory<Program>, created in [OneTimeSetUp] and disposed in [OneTimeTearDown]) when routing, binding, middleware, authentication, DI, repositories, the ORM or database persistence is what the test must prove.
Tests start from a known state and own their setup; they never depend on development seed data or on the order of other tests.
Do not generate low-value tests merely to raise a coverage percentage.
Use descriptive test names stating scenario/condition and expected behavior (e.g. MethodOrScenario_Condition_ExpectedBehavior); follow an established project convention when one exists.

The backend follows Clean Architecture with the role-to-project mapping: domain model = backend/<Name>.Domain; use-case layer with Application Services, persistence-access contracts and the commit boundary IUnitOfWork = <Name>.Application; implementation layer (persistence and external adapters) = <Name>.Infrastructure; entry point and composition root (Program.cs) = <Name>.Api; test projects <Name>.Application.Tests and <Name>.IntegrationTests (optional Domain.Tests, Infrastructure.Tests).

Do not introduce CQRS command/query handlers, mediator libraries or mediator-based request dispatch, Vertical Slice Architecture or similar mediator-based organization unless explicitly approved; a service growing too large is a signal to reconsider its responsibilities, not a reason to adopt another pattern.
Keep Domain free of persistence-implementation, web-framework/transport-implementation, HTTP and external-service implementation concerns.

Simple domain entities by default; straightforward CRUD and workflow rules (validation, immutable fields, status transitions, allowed or forbidden edits) belong in Application Services and do not by themselves justify a Rich Domain Model.

Move behavior into Domain only when non-trivial domain invariants or behavior materially benefit from domain-level encapsulation independently of one use case; otherwise a Rich Domain Model or DDD tactical pattern requires approval unless the approved specification already requires it.

Do not add factory methods, private setters, transition methods, Aggregate Roots, Domain Events, Specifications, Domain Services, systematic Value Objects or similar constructs merely to make a simple model look domain-driven.
Application Services orchestrate use cases; they may coordinate Domain objects, repositories, external-service abstractions and the Unit of Work.

Do not duplicate equivalent DTOs across Api and Application merely to create layer-shaped types; add transport-specific request/response contracts in Api when separation from Application models gives a concrete boundary benefit.
Entry-point adapters in Api (controllers) are the default HTTP entry point and stay thin: they bind and validate HTTP input, invoke Application Services and translate outcomes into HTTP responses.
Entry-point adapters must not contain business logic, access the persistence context or concrete repositories, or construct infrastructure services manually.

Prefer specific repository interfaces representing cohesive Application persistence needs over generic CRUD contracts mirroring tables; interfaces live in Application, implementations in Infrastructure.

Application must not depend on IGenericRepository<T> or another generic CRUD contract; a generic repository base class may exist only inside Infrastructure, only to remove real duplication, and never as a replacement for the ORM's query capabilities.

IUnitOfWork (defined in Application) is the normal commit boundary of a use case; repositories stage changes and Application Services decide when to commit; the implementation delegates to AppDbContext.SaveChangesAsync and staged changes are the shared context's tracked changes.

Repositories taking part in one use case share the same scoped Unit of Work and persistence context (the scoped AppDbContext); inject repositories explicitly; IUnitOfWork must not become a repository container or service locator.
Do not introduce explicit transaction APIs until a concrete use case needs control beyond a single commit through IUnitOfWork.

HTTP status codes and transport response semantics belong to the entry point; the use-case layer and domain model must not return transport result types (IActionResult, ActionResult<T>, IResult) or HTTP status codes.

Represent common expected outcomes explicitly when useful (null, bool, a typed outcome) but do not force a generic result-wrapper pattern and do not name use-case outcome categories after HTTP statuses; the entry point maps outcomes to HTTP.
Keep cache technology out of the domain model and do not leak infrastructure cache APIs into the use-case layer without a deliberate boundary abstraction.

The implementation layer translates remote HTTP responses (HttpResponseMessage, headers, status) into use-case-layer abstractions; remote transport response objects and other remote transport concerns must not leak into the use-case layer.
Do not create separate domain or persistence models merely because the public API has several versions; isolate version-specific transport contracts at the entry point when practical.

Use FluentValidation for explicit request and use-case validation where appropriate and keep each rule at its owning boundary (transport concerns at the entry point, use-case rules in the use-case layer, domain invariants in the domain model); do not move domain invariants into validators or duplicate one rule mechanically across layers.

Swagger/OpenAPI metadata describes the API that actually runs (routes, important response statuses including pipeline-produced ones, schemas, authentication behavior); never document speculative responses.
Enable Swagger UI in Development; exposure in other environments follows the Swagger decision (only when deployment requirements explicitly justify it).
When Serilog is configured use the DI-integrated AddSerilog approach with provider configuration in environment-aware configuration; application code keeps depending on ILogger<T>.
Production containers use an appropriate runtime image rather than the SDK image for convenience and do not switch to root merely to bypass filesystem permission problems.
The entry-point mechanism is ASP.NET Core Controllers (controller classes in a Controllers/ folder of the entry-point project); do not create Minimal API endpoint groups unless explicitly requested.
Use modern standalone Angular APIs for new code and organize application code primarily by feature.
Use Signals for naturally synchronous, local UI state and RxJS when asynchronous streams, HTTP composition, cancellation or event pipelines make it clearer; avoid mechanical conversions.
Prefer functional interceptors for new code; keep interceptor responsibilities cross-cutting and never put feature business logic in an interceptor.
Avoid manual nested RxJS subscriptions; prefer composition operators when stream composition expresses the behavior clearly.
When manually subscribing from framework-managed code, tie the subscription lifetime to the component or service lifecycle using the project's current Angular facilities.

EF Core is an implementation-layer detail: use its full capabilities inside the persistence implementation but never leak EF Core concepts into the use-case layer; do not cripple repository implementations to preserve a generic abstraction.

Persistence-access contracts must not expose IQueryable<T>, DbSet<T>, DbContext, EF Core expressions or provider-specific types; LINQ-to-EF query construction stays in the persistence implementation and contracts return materialized entities, collections, projections or explicit result models.

For an empty Development database maintain a small, deterministic, representative seed dataset covering the main meaningful states and relationships (new, active, completed, archived; with and without optional values; boundary states); no exhaustive combinations or random bulk data.
Development seeding is a persistence-implementation/bootstrap concern: it may use AppDbContext directly and need not go through persistence-access contracts or the commit boundary.
Keep substantial seed construction in a dedicated internal DbSeeder exposed through a narrow initialization extension, not in Program.cs, AppDbContext, entity configurations or migrations.
Automatic seeding runs only in the Development environment; never seed Production automatically; tests never use the seeder.
The seeder must not call Database.Migrate() or EnsureCreated() or otherwise create or upgrade schema; migrations are applied separately before seeding.
When an approved technology exists in the decisions file, use it rather than silently selecting an alternative; replacing it is Reserved (record with architecture-decision).
Backend platform: .NET 10 LTS (latest stable servicing release), C# 14, ASP.NET Core, ASP.NET Core Controllers; moving to a preview/RC .NET or C# release requires approval.
FluentValidation is the standard explicit request/use-case validation library; application logging uses ILogger<T> with Serilog as the provider.

Swashbuckle Swagger UI is the interactive API documentation and manual-testing surface for Development (/swagger); expose it outside Development only when deployment requirements explicitly justify it.
Microsoft resilience packages are approved only when a real integration needs resilience.
Use the .slnx solution format; legacy .sln only when an external tool or project requirement needs it.
Use repository-level Directory.Build.props for genuinely shared .NET build settings and Directory.Packages.props for Central Package Management; project-specific settings stay in their own projects.
Do not introduce Docker merely because the application can be containerized; add container artifacts only when the project or deployment needs them.
Persistence is EF Core with Microsoft SQL Server (Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer); provider-specific concerns stay out of the use-case layer and domain model.
Backend testing: NUnit; backend test projects live under backend/ beside production projects; WebApplicationFactory<Program> is the integration-test baseline; Testcontainers is conditional.

appsettings.Development.json provides a usable local Development connection string whenever it contains no secret credentials (e.g. LocalDB with Trusted_Connection); when local SQL Server requires credentials keep the non-secret structure in configuration and supply the credential-bearing value through user-secrets or another approved local secret mechanism.

Level model of the instruction system: every artifact is placed by stability (0-core, 1-architecture, 2-technology, 3-project) and starts with a one-line header (Level, optional Capability/Facet, Owns, Scope, Loading); conformance dependencies point only to the same or a more stable level; Core and Architecture name no concrete implementation technology in any form, pointers included, except the fixed platform vocabulary (.NET, C#, TypeScript, Git, HTTP; ASP.NET Core and NuGet are not exempt) and refer to Level 2 only by role, capability, facet or a technology-neutral skill name; every artifact is listed in the instruction map, and check-instructions is run after any change.
trigger_scope: authoring or changing instruction artifacts (template maintenance)
why_extra_or_uncertain: Instruction-system organization rule of the L1 template; the oracle defines no level hierarchy, header format or technology-neutrality requirement for instruction files.

normative_action: Static capability composition: exactly four slots (architecture required frame; persistence and backend-testing required leaves; frontend optional leaf); each required slot has exactly one selected implementation and the optional slot zero or one; only selected modules ship; module-owned artifacts declare Capability: and appear in their MODULE.md; a <slot>.<facet> reference resolves through the selection record and a cleared optional slot (none) means its facets do not apply.
trigger_scope: template capability structure and selection record
why_extra_or_uncertain: No oracle policy defines capability slots, their cardinality or a selection record; ARC-020/DEP-009 only fix the approved stack and require approval to change it.

normative_action: Hooks are registered in exec form (command node with the script path as argument data, no shell); the critical PreToolUse gate sets onFailure block so a missing script, crash, timeout or malformed input blocks the command; PostToolUse and Stop hooks stay non-blocking.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Hook-configuration design of the template; no oracle policy regulates how instruction-system hooks are registered or how they fail.

normative_action: Use npm for the frontend workspace unless the project deliberately adopts another package manager; keep package-lock.json consistent with package.json; place build/test tooling in devDependencies rather than runtime dependencies without a reason.
Commit package.json and package-lock.json.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Read as a version-control content convention (both files belong in the repository) the clause is entailed by DEP-007; read as an instruction to perform commits it conflicts with GOV-015, which allows commits only on explicit request. The text does not resolve which reading is meant.

normative_action: Instruction inventory integrity: the required workflow skills (development-workflow, project-structure, verify, code-review, build-fix, custom-settings, git-workflow, security-scan, add-dependency, architecture-decision, template-maintenance), the shared knowledge skills (http-api, aspnet-error-handling, logging, httpclient-factory, configuration, dependency-injection, caching, swagger, api-versioning, health-check, docker, ci-cd, modern-csharp, authentication) and each selected module's knowledge skill exist; a skill's frontmatter name equals its directory and it has a description; template-maintenance is user-only (disable-model-invocation: true) and every other skill stays model-invocable; named skill/agent references and .claude path references resolve; skill-private references are used only by their owning skill.
trigger_scope: template maintenance of .claude/skills, agents and references
exceptions: The instruction map may list private references.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Inventory and invocation invariants of the template; no oracle policy requires particular skills to exist or fixes their invocation mode.

normative_action: Reserved decisions need explicit approval: changing an accepted project/architecture decision; adopting a new architectural style or pattern (Rich Domain Model or DDD tactical patterns, CQRS, mediator-based organization, Vertical Slice Architecture, event sourcing, a project-wide Result model, microservices); adding a production project/layer; changing persistence boundaries (e.g. several persistence contexts) or persistence technology; adding an infrastructure category (messaging, background processing, distributed cache, search, external storage, external identity); adding a major library/framework or replacing approved baseline technology; introducing a project-wide convention or abstraction; changing authentication/authorization architecture; a breaking public API change.
Add the Asp.Versioning Controller integration (Asp.Versioning.Mvc, Asp.Versioning.Mvc.ApiExplorer) only once Controller API versioning has actually been adopted.

Before installing check whether the exact package/version is deprecated, check known vulnerability information (dotnet package list --vulnerable --include-transitive, the frontend audit command) and verify the exact selected version's license from official registry metadata (and upstream when necessary); permissive licenses (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD) are acceptable without approval; being free to download does not make a package acceptable.

Do not install automatically when a package requires payment or a commercial license, or its license has material obligations or cannot be confidently classified (strong copyleft, dual licensing, source-available/custom terms, unclear or missing); present the concern and reasonable alternatives (say so explicitly when none exists), never substitute silently, and make no legal conclusions beyond published license information.

Keep changes focused on the requested scope and preserve existing behavior unless the task or approved specification requires a change; e.g. after a scanner finding do not automatically replace or upgrade unrelated packages, and do not perform unrelated dependency cleanup during a narrow task.
exceptions: Task or approved specification requires change.

normative_action: Prefer simple, maintainable solutions; keep architectural complexity proportional to current requirements; avoid speculative abstractions (e.g. do not wrap every UI-library component in a custom abstraction without a reason).

When generated output is wrong or its source contract changes, fix or update the authoritative source (contract, generator configuration) and regenerate; keep generated code separate from handwritten code and do not hand-edit disposable generated output unless the repository intentionally treats it as maintained source.
exceptions: Generated output intentionally maintained as source.

normative_action: When deprecating an externally consumed API version, mark the deprecation in versioning metadata, document the replacement, communicate a realistic migration/removal timeline and keep the old version working for the promised support period; never silently remove a deprecated version.

For a Reserved decision send a Decision Request (Context, Options, Recommendation, Blocked, Proceeding with) and continue only with non-Reserved work; do not ask approval for routine choices already constrained by the specification, approved stack, existing code or rules.
In autonomous or headless runs take only a policy-compliant non-Reserved path and list unresolved Decision Requests in the final report instead of deciding.
When a new behavioral rule or tunable value is approved, update the durable source of truth: product behavior in SPECIFICATION.md, tunable values in CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md (then custom-settings).
Remove dependencies that are no longer used when that is part of the current change and safe to verify; do not leave dead references.
exceptions: Unrelated dependency cleanup during a narrow task is excluded.
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-001 restricts adding dependencies and GOV-014 limits scope; no oracle policy requires removing dependencies made unused by a change.

normative_action: The add-dependency workflow reports package, version, license, vulnerability/deprecation result, target project and approvals obtained or still pending.
why_extra_or_uncertain: WF-009 covers verification reporting; no oracle policy prescribes dependency-specific report contents.

normative_action: Adopting API versioning is Reserved and needs explicit approval, even when a concrete compatibility need exists.
why_extra_or_uncertain: API-013 allows introducing versioning when a real compatibility need exists and does not require approval; the oracle's consequential-change list does not name API versioning adoption.

normative_action: Every approved Reserved decision is recorded as an ADR at docs/decisions/NNNN-<kebab-title>.md (Status Accepted with date, Approved by, Context, Decision, Consequences, Alternatives considered; docs/decisions/ created with the first ADR) and summarized as a decision line pointing to the ADR in the decision file of the owning level (frame style rule, decisions.md, frontend stack rule), never in a single cross-level register and without restating rules that live elsewhere.
exceptions: Product behavior and tunable values go to SPECIFICATION.md / CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md instead.
why_extra_or_uncertain: GOV-017 requires approval for Reserved changes but no recording artifact; GOV-007 covers product behavior sources only. No oracle policy requires ADR documents or level-stratified decision summaries.

normative_action: The architecture-decision workflow reports the decision, ADR path, decision files updated and follow-up work (structure, dependencies, migrations).
why_extra_or_uncertain: No oracle policy prescribes decision-recording report contents.

normative_action: Do not introduce frameworks, libraries, infrastructure or architectural patterns (e.g. identity/JWT/OIDC infrastructure, pipeline stages, distributed caches) without a concrete current need.

Build-fix starts from reproduction and diagnosis: reproduce the actual failure with the narrowest reliable command, read the complete output, group errors by root cause and fix root causes before downstream symptoms; when tests fail decide whether production code, setup, expectation, environment or an intentional contract change is at fault; determine the authoritative contract instead of patching both sides of a cross-stack break into inconsistent shapes; never fabricate replacement APIs.

Repair in small bounded iterations: after each meaningful fix rerun the narrowest failing check, widen verification only after the focused failure is resolved, do not run unrelated build systems, use several focused attempts rather than an unlimited loop, stop and reassess when progress stalls and never repeat variants of a failed guess.

Repairs never bypass architecture: no invalid or outward project references to make a type compile, persistence types in the use-case layer, business logic in entry points, client-only authorization or HTTP calls scattered into components; preserve architecture and project conventions while fixing.

When verification fails make the smallest appropriate fix and rerun until green or genuine user input is required; never claim a problem fixed while a known relevant failure remains, never leave the repository knowingly worse, and when a required toolchain is unavailable report the limitation instead of editing source or changing declared SDK/runtime versions to compensate.
exceptions: Unrelated pre-existing failures are left alone unless they block verification or the user asks.

normative_action: A behavioral probe that uniquely establishes correct behavior is preserved in maintained automated coverage (verify step 4) unless equivalent coverage exists; build, compiler and static-analysis runs do not require new tests.
Report the actual verification state with PASS / NOT RUN / NOT APPLICABLE per area; never imply that an unchecked area passed.

CI definitions stay in source control, reproduce the repository's supported build/test commands for the parts that actually exist (no assumed providers, containers or tooling; no optional formatter turned into a gate without adoption), restore from a clean environment without developer-machine state, and keep build/test failures visible.

Review reports concrete defects or risks prioritized as correctness; security and authorization; data integrity and persistence; architectural boundary violations; concurrency and integration; missing meaningful tests; maintainability; evidence-supported performance; style preferences are never ranked above behavioral defects; the reviewer does not rewrite working code, report tooling-owned formatting, demand personal style or unadopted patterns, recommend speculative optimizations, or add filler praise.

Do not manufacture findings to populate categories or invent failures without a plausible execution path; when there are no meaningful findings say so and name important areas that could not be verified.
When SPECIFICATION.md is non-empty it is authoritative for project-specific functional requirements and observable product behavior (the product contract); an empty template file is intentional.

CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md holds approved project-level tunable limits and defaults (maximum lengths, page sizes, retention periods, numeric thresholds) recorded under stable descriptive names with value and purpose; SPECIFICATION.md owns behavioral intent; approved values are intended behavior.

Do not silently weaken, contradict or materially extend approved behavior, and do not invent user-visible behavior, limits, defaults, restrictions or workflows (new limits, reserved values, required fields, extra validation, observable string semantics) because they seem reasonable or were not forbidden.
exceptions: User-approved details with synchronized durable sources.

normative_action: Run architecture, formatting/analyzer, dependency and security checks when relevant to the change rather than indiscriminately (e.g. the architecture check when project references or packages changed).
For a meaningful bug with plausible recurrence add a regression test unless equivalent coverage already exists; do not request duplicate tests.

Compiler diagnostics, analyzers, scanners and repository tools are evidence, not authority; no MCP server or specific analyzer is required for review to work; read the code before turning a tool warning into a finding.
SPECIFICATION.md and CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md must not contradict each other; if they appear to conflict, stop and ask which source must be corrected before touching implementation.

When an approved CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md value is added, changed or removed, identify and update every affected surface (owning code, validators and request constraints, domain/use-case checks, database mapping, frontend validation and hints, tests and test data, documentation, mirrored configuration), search for stale references, keep frontend validation synchronized while backend stays authoritative, change only affected behavior, and run the normal verification; a single changed literal does not establish synchronization.

Never store secrets, environment-specific connection details, package versions, HTTP status codes, ports, migration identifiers or incidental implementation constants (including framework defaults not intentionally overridden) in CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md.
Register FluentValidation validators with the FluentValidation.DependencyInjectionExtensions package and follow the project's established invocation pattern instead of adding a competing mechanism.
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-010 fixes FluentValidation as the library and API-010 the validation boundaries; no oracle policy prescribes the registration package.

normative_action: The build-fix report states the initial failure, root cause, changes made, backend build / frontend build / tests status (PASS, NOT RUN, NOT APPLICABLE) and remaining issues.
why_extra_or_uncertain: WF-009 requires reporting actual verification states; it does not prescribe failure/root-cause/change sections.

normative_action: Do not cache tracked ORM entities across commit boundaries (named caching anti-pattern).
why_extra_or_uncertain: RUN-021 governs invalidation consistency and ARC-019 confines the ORM to the implementation layer; caching tracked entities is an ORM technique pitfall (EXC-011 class) that the template elevates to a named prohibition.

normative_action: Code-review output gives for each finding severity, file/location, what is wrong, why it matters and the smallest reasonable fix, ordered by severity on the scale Critical (data loss, security vulnerability, reliably broken core behavior; blocks merge), High (likely defect or architecture/data-integrity issue; fix before merge), Medium (real maintainability, robustness or test gap), Low (non-blocking improvement).
why_extra_or_uncertain: WF-011/WF-012 prescribe priorities and no manufactured findings; the oracle sets no output format or severity scale.

normative_action: The custom-settings workflow reports the setting, old -> new value, every surface updated and the verify result.
why_extra_or_uncertain: No oracle policy prescribes settings-change report contents.

normative_action: For a new application or substantial feature read SPECIFICATION.md (and CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md) before planning or implementing.

Before implementing a questionable request name the concrete concerns (duplication, poor cohesion, trigger or loading problems, context cost, architecture conflict, unnecessary complexity) and propose an alternative; this never authorizes silently rewriting or ignoring the user's requirement.

A performance-motivated change identifies the actual bottleneck, preserves observable behavior, uses the simplest optimization that addresses it, adds or keeps tests for affected behavior, and benchmarks or profiles non-obvious or complex optimizations.
For substantial feature work or a newly implemented application run code-review (or the code-reviewer agent) before final verification.
Before declaring implementation complete (and before preparing a PR) run verify at the scope and risk of the change; work is not complete until its verify step has run.
Do not commit, push, merge, rebase, reset, force-push, delete or rename branches, or perform other repository-changing Git operations unless explicitly requested.
Parallel implementation work uses separate branches or worktrees (one branch is never checked out in several normal worktrees); keep unrelated changes out of the current branch.

Never discard, overwrite, reset, clean, stash away or otherwise destroy user work to make a Git operation easier; never remove a worktree holding uncommitted user work; never stash, reset or discard automatically to let a merge or rebase proceed.

Before any repository-changing operation inspect the relevant state (status, diffs, current branch, upstream, what high-risk operations would lose or rewrite) and use the minimum operation that achieves the request; never silently clean unrelated working-tree changes.

Before committing inspect the staged diff and include only the requested logical change; never stage unrelated modified files; one logical change per commit with implementation and its tests together; no unrelated fixes bundled; avoid pushing unrelated local commits.

High-risk Git operations (reset --hard, clean, push --force, push --force-with-lease, branch deletion, rebasing shared history) run only when explicitly requested or required by an approved workflow, and only after inspecting what will be lost or rewritten.
why_extra_or_uncertain: GOV-015 allows repository-changing Git operations only on explicit request; the alternative trigger 'required by an approved workflow' names no such workflow and could authorize high-risk operations without an explicit request, or could merely refer to an explicitly approved procedure. The relation to GOV-015 cannot be settled from the text.

normative_action: The development-workflow output summarizes what changed, Delegated decisions taken, open Decision Requests (Reserved) and the verify report.
why_extra_or_uncertain: WF-009 covers verification state and GOV-017 reporting of unresolved Decision Requests in headless runs; listing Delegated decisions in every implementation summary is an additional reporting duty.

normative_action: Treat main, master and other protected or shared branches as non-rewritable.
why_extra_or_uncertain: GOV-015 permits repository-changing operations, including force-push and rebase, when explicitly requested; this rule forbids rewriting these branches without an approval path.

normative_action: A pull request stays focused and its description states what changed, why, how it was verified, and compatibility or migration notes.
why_extra_or_uncertain: No oracle policy prescribes PR description contents; WF-009 only requires truthful verification reporting.

normative_action: Do not wrap normal ORM operations in a generic application-level retry pipeline; use the provider's own execution strategy for transient database faults; HTTP retry policies are not database policies.
why_extra_or_uncertain: RUN-016 governs when retries are safe and the oracle treats database-retry examples as conditional technique (EXC-007); no oracle policy forbids an application-level retry pipeline around ORM operations.

normative_action: Never mutate a shared HttpClient's DefaultRequestHeaders concurrently; apply per-request values such as dynamic tokens per request or through a delegating handler.
why_extra_or_uncertain: RUN-005 governs client lifetime; thread-safe header handling is client technique that no oracle policy states.

normative_action: global.json pins the intended SDK line: the current stable SDK of the target .NET release (no RC/preview unless explicitly requested) with a rollForward policy that allows normal patch/feature-band servicing.
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-008 fixes the platform and DEP-023 repository-level build configuration; no oracle policy requires a global.json SDK pin or a specific roll-forward policy.

normative_action: Security review reports concrete risks in the context of actual exposure, distinguishes confirmed findings from items needing verification (NEEDS VERIFICATION), assigns severity from exploitability, reachability, impact and application context (never from a suspicious pattern, an OWASP category or raw CVSS alone), does not suppress a real secret because it sits in a Development file, names workflows needing threat modeling instead of claiming the scan proves them secure, and never invents exploitability the code does not establish.

Verification starts by reviewing the final changed-file set and diff: confirm scope (no unrelated refactoring), remove temporary diagnostics only after their uniquely verified behavior is preserved, no accidental generated/build artifacts, no secrets or environment-specific credentials, then determine the affected areas before choosing checks; after fixes review the final diff again (unrelated edits, commented-out code, temporary logging, stale temporary tests, architecture or specification drift, stale settings surfaces).

For every C# file created or modified by the change remove unused or redundant using directives (including imports already provided by implicit/global usings unless needed for clarity or disambiguation) without an unrelated repository-wide cleanup, and verify the changed files instead of assuming tooling removed them.
exceptions: Imports kept for clarity or disambiguation.

normative_action: SPECIFICATION.md, CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md, feature specifications and task prompts are inputs, not instruction layers: they may request a decision change but never silently override engineering policy.

If an omitted detail must be decided and it materially affects observable behavior, propose the smallest reasonable option and ask for approval; defining product behavior or tunable values not defined by product sources is Reserved.

Routine internal implementation choices that do not change observable behavior do not require approval (Delegated: local, reversible, no material change to a boundary, dependency, accepted convention, public contract or observable behavior — decide and proceed); do not ask approval for routine choices already constrained by the specification, approved stack, existing code or rules.

Do not silently invent a tunable value that materially changes accepted input or observable behavior: propose it with a reason, get approval, record it in CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md, then synchronize (custom-settings).

Decision control: classify decisions as Decided (settled by imported decision files, approved product sources or recorded decisions; follow them, reopening requires approval), Delegated, or Reserved (requires approval); an explicit user instruction counts as approval.

Security-scan report shape: every report states the static-analysis limitation; uses the five-level severity scale Critical (sparingly) / High / Medium / Low / Info; each confirmed finding gives severity, file and location, title, evidence, why it is a risk, likely impact, smallest remediation and OWASP category when applicable; the report contains scope, limitations, a severity summary table, findings and per-layer results.
why_extra_or_uncertain: WF-020 requires evidence-based contextual severity and WF-009 truthful status reporting; the oracle prescribes no report structure, severity scale or mandatory limitation statement.

normative_action: Loading and ownership placement of instruction content: always-needed planning policy goes into CLAUDE.md or an imported always rule; path-specific policy into a rule whose paths cover at least its scope; procedure obligations into the owning workflow; each rule has one owner (elsewhere only a pointer or a yes/no check naming the owner); the always-loaded surface (CLAUDE.md, its imports, skill descriptions) stays compact — path or workflow policy is not moved into it and always-needed policy is not moved out of it to save tokens.
why_extra_or_uncertain: Instruction-system placement rules; the oracle does not regulate where instruction content is loaded or owned.

normative_action: Unclear-case test: any 'yes' makes a decision Reserved — does it add, remove or replace a dependency, framework or infrastructure capability; change a project/layer/reference boundary; establish a convention other code must follow; change observable behavior or a public contract; become expensive to reverse once other code depends on it?
why_extra_or_uncertain: GOV-017 requires a Decided/Delegated/Reserved classification but not this test; under it any unclear dependency addition or removal becomes Reserved, whereas the oracle allows dependencies with a concrete need (DEP-001) and delegates routine internal choices (GOV-005).

normative_action: Repository-wide Directory.Build.props enables nullable reference types and implicit usings for every .NET project (target framework net10.0).
why_extra_or_uncertain: DEP-023 places shared settings in Directory.Build.props and DEP-008 fixes the platform; no oracle policy requires nullable reference types or implicit usings.
